response.sql: SELECT AVG(g.group_avg) AS avg_of_group_avgs FROM (SELECT e.ordersmark, o.orderflow, AVG(e.fillcount) AS group_avg FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark WHERE e.expirespot > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND e.expirespot < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.orderflow) g;

assumptions.assumption: recordvault is unique in orders, as the documentation states, so each execution joins to at most one order. The schema does not enforce this.

expirespot is stored as text in a fixed-width 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' form, so text comparison matches chronological order. The schema declares it as text(6), which conflicts with the documented timestamp type and could truncate values; if so, the window filter would be wrong.

Executions with a NULL expirespot are excluded by the range filter. Executions with NULL fillcount are ignored by AVG, and a group with only NULL fillcounts drops out of the outer average. An empty result returns NULL.
